chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadala, from Abu al-Maghra', from Sama'a, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the slaughtered meat of the Jew and the Christian, so he said: 'Do not approach it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating the meat of Jews and Christians?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a clear prohibition against consuming the meat of Jews and Christians, using the emphatic phrase 'Do not approach it' (La taqrabannahā). This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that their slaughter lacks the necessary invocation of Allah's name, distinguishing it from the permissibility granted to Christians in the Quran, which many Shia jurists interpret as conditional or specific to certain contexts.
